H.answer: No, the Supreme Court in McCray v. United States (ID: 195_0027-01) did not hold that federal excise taxes on artificially colored oleomargarine violate tenth amendment reserved state revenue powers. Instead, the Court held that the judiciary is without authority to avoid an act of Congress lawfully exerting the taxing power, even if the tax seems unwise or oppressive, and that Congress has the power to tax and select the objects upon which the tax shall be levied. The Court also stated that nothing in the Fifth or Tenth Amendments operates to take away the grant of power to tax conferred by the Constitution upon Congress.
